topic: Abstract Vector Spaces: Moving Beyond Arrows

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Concrete Vector
lecture_lines: Traditionally, we visualize vectors as arrows in space.
We can add arrows by placing them head-to-tail.
We can scale arrows by stretching or shrinking them.
animations: Draw a 2D vector arrow (3, 2) in light blue (#00CCFF) labeled 'v'.
Animate vector addition using head-to-tail method with another vector (1, 1) in light green (#00FF00) labeled 'w'.
Show scalar multiplication by stretching the original 'v' vector by a factor of 2, changing its color to yellow (#FFFF00).

sections.title: The Concept of Abstraction
lecture_lines: Vectors are not just arrows; they are rule followers.
A vector space is a collection of compatible objects.
Adding or scaling these objects keeps them within the set.
animations: Display a set of abstract shapes inside a container labeled 'Vector Space' (#FFFFFF).
Animate two shapes merging (addition) to form a new shape within the container in light purple (#DDA0DD).
Animate a shape being scaled (changing size) while remaining within the container in light orange (#FFDAB9).

sections.title: The 8 Axioms: The Rules of the Game
lecture_lines: Eight formal axioms define what makes a vector space.
Commutativity ensures the order of addition does not matter.
Every space must contain a unique zero vector.
Adding the zero vector leaves any object unchanged.
These rules apply to any set passing the test.
animations: Show a list of 8 axiom names appearing one by one in light gray (#CCCCCC).
Highlight 'Commutativity' (#FFD700) and show u + v = v + u swapping positions visually.
Highlight 'Zero Vector' (#FF4500) and show a vector v added to a zero point, resulting in v unchanged.
Highlight 'Distributive' (#1E90FF) and show c(u+v) = cu + cv expanding with color-coded variables.
Apply a checkmark to all items and label the space 'Valid Vector Space' in bright green (#32CD32).

sections.title: Exotic Examples: Functions as Vectors
lecture_lines: Functions can be treated as vectors in abstract spaces.
Adding two functions creates a new, combined curve.
Scaling a function changes its height or amplitude.
Like arrows, functions satisfy all eight vector axioms.
This transforms calculus into a branch of linear algebra.
animations: Plot two sine wave curves: one in pink (#FF69B4) and one in cyan (#00FFFF).
Animate the addition of these waves (superposition) to create a new purple wave (#8A2BE2).
Scale the pink wave by increasing its amplitude to show scalar multiplication in action.

sections.title: Why it Matters: The Power of Generalization
lecture_lines: Abstract proofs apply to arrows, functions, and matrices.
One theorem can solve problems across many fields.
This generalization is the core power of linear algebra.
animations: Show icons for Physics (atom), Economics (graph), and AI (nodes) in white (#FFFFFF).
Display a central 'Master Key' labeled 'Linear Algebra' in gold (#FFD700).
Animate the key unlocking all three icons simultaneously, turning them green (#00FF00) to show generalization.
